relevance_note: The report ties an in-scope person to a TNFAIP3 variant, “WES of the proband uncovered a novel variant inTNFAIP3 (Chr6(GRCh38): g.137871292G>A; NM_001270507.1: c.65G>A; p.(Arg22Gln))”, carried by the proband and two affected relatives, although the authors classify it as a variant of uncertain significance and never diagnose HA20.
method_note: Case report of one family; the Markdown has no tables and no Supplementary material section, so every cell comes from the narrative text, read and typed by hand (no script transcribed anything). Four in-scope people: the proband (never given a label other than 'the proband'/'the patient', so labelled 'P1' under rules 5-6), his mother, his daughter and his sister. The proband's father is mentioned once ('the proband's father was deceased') with no individual-level fact beyond that and no variant, so he has no row; his carrier status was not assessed. The paper uses no family number: 'Family 1' was entered only because the schema asks for a family label, taken from the single pedigree (Figure 1) - this is a made-up value and is the weakest cell in the file. Figure 1 is not available in the Markdown, so the pedigree could not be read; 'An arrow indicates the proband' is the only basis for is_proband. The proband's heterozygous zygosity rests on the abstract sentence 'revealed a heterozygous variant of uncertain significance in exon 2 ofTNFAIP3 ... in all affected members' (a named group that includes him), not on a sentence about him alone; the abstract also places the variant in 'exon 2'. Inheritance is 'not reported' for everyone: the mother was tested and negative and the father was deceased and untested, so neither 'de novo' nor 'inherited' is stated. Variant type 'missense' comes from the general statements 'no known association between missense variants inTNFAIP3' and the title ('a Missense Variant'), which do not name a group of people; it is recorded anyway because the variant is printed as a semiconservative amino acid substitution p.(Arg22Gln)/p.R22Q - this derivation from the protein change is flagged as an uncertainty, and a strict reading of D-29 would make it 'not reported'. For the daughter and sister the cDNA string 'c.65G>A' has no individual-level span: the paper says only that the p.R22Q variant (or 'the variant of uncertain significance' in the abstract) was found in them, so their cDNA value is quoted from a group statement and their gene symbol from the abstract sentence. GJB2 rows are included because the paper attributes that variant unambiguously to the proband and his mother ('in the proband and his mother only'); its frameshift class comes from the printed 'fs' protein notation, and the proband's GJB2 zygosity was left 'not reported' because the only 'heterozygous' statement names the mother. Normal/negative findings were recorded per D-27 as the abnormality ruled out (mastocytosis, and the normal bone marrow biopsy, CBC and TSH written as the paper writes them, since a normal investigation as a whole excludes nothing more specific than what it names). Checklist statuses: 'skin lesions (rash, folliculitis, erythema nodosum)' was marked observed for the proband, daughter and sister from the title phrase 'a Family with Chronic Urticaria and Angioedema' (urticaria is a rash); this is debatable and could be 'not reported'. The proband's fever during his attacks was not counted as 'recurrent fever' in the checklist because recurrence is not stated, so that item stays 'not reported' while a phenotypic_features row records the fever. 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)' was marked observed for the proband from 'His anti-IgE receptor antibody was elevated at 18.5%'. 'elevated inflammatory markers (CRP/ESR)' was left 'not reported' everywhere because no CRP or ESR value is printed. No contradictions were found between sections. No group statement was used to exclude any feature, and no study criteria were used.

treatment_summary.value: antihistamines levocetirizine, cetirizine, fexofenadine, and loratadine; prednisone and steroid injections cleared the hives but prednisone was stopped due to side effects; a future trial of anti-IgE therapy (omalizumab) was suggested
span: The proband tried numerous treatment modalities to suppress his urticaria, including the following antihistamines: levocetirizine, cetirizine, fexofenadine, and loratadine. Prednisone and steroid injections were the only treatments that cleared the patient's hives; however, treatment with prednisone was eventually stopped due to side effects.
Many patients with chronic urticaria improve with anti-IgE therapy (omalizumab), suggesting that inappropriate activation of mast cells and basophils may play a role in disease pathogenesis.

span: Due to the absence of mast cells in the bone marrow biopsy, the patient did not meet diagnostic criteria for mastocytosis and was ultimately diagnosed with chronic urticaria.
WES of the proband uncovered a novel variant inTNFAIP3 (Chr6(GRCh38): g.137871292G>A; NM_001270507.1: c.65G>A; p.(Arg22Gln)), which could possibly correlate with the proband's disease phenotype.
Based on the ACMG 2015 guidelines, the c.65G>A (p.R22Q) variant was classified as a variant of uncertain significance (VUS) [23].
